Solution to the exercise in [Lecture 10](../slides/lecture10.pdf).

We observe four ones, three zeros, and two missing values. Let $\theta_n$ be the
current estimate of the Bernoulli success probability.

## E-step

Conditional on the observed values, each missing $X_i$ still has expectation
$\theta_n$. The expected complete-data log-likelihood is therefore
$$
  Q(\theta \mid \theta_n) = (4 + 2\theta_n)\log(\theta)
                            + \bigl(3 + 2(1 - \theta_n)\bigr)\log(1 - \theta).
$$

## M-step

Maximizing $Q$ gives the expected fraction of ones among all nine entries:
$$
  \theta_{n+1} = \frac{4 + 2\theta_n}{9}.
$$

The fixed point solves $9\hat{\theta} = 4 + 2\hat{\theta}$, so
$\hat{\theta} = 4/7$. This is also the observed-data MLE: only the seven
observed values contribute to the likelihood, and four of them are ones.

## Implementation

```{r}
#| label: bernoulli-em-solution

x <- c(1, 0, 1, NA, 0, NA, 1, 1, 0)

fit_bernoulli_em <- function(x, start, iterations = 6) {
  observed <- x[!is.na(x)]
  n_missing <- sum(is.na(x))
  loglik <- function(theta) {
    sum(observed * log(theta) + (1 - observed) * log1p(-theta))
  }

  path <- numeric(iterations + 1)
  path[1] <- start
  for (iteration in seq_len(iterations)) {
    path[iteration + 1] <- (sum(observed) +
      n_missing * path[iteration]) /
      length(x)
  }

  data.frame(
    iteration = 0:iterations,
    theta = path,
    loglik = vapply(path, loglik, numeric(1))
  )
}

from_half <- fit_bernoulli_em(x, start = 0.5)
from_tenth <- fit_bernoulli_em(x, start = 0.1)

data.frame(
  iteration = from_half$iteration,
  theta_from_0.5 = round(from_half$theta, 6),
  loglik_from_0.5 = round(from_half$loglik, 6),
  theta_from_0.1 = round(from_tenth$theta, 6),
  loglik_from_0.1 = round(from_tenth$loglik, 6)
)
```

Both paths approach $4/7$, and the observed-data log-likelihood increases at
each step. The update also shows the exact error contraction:
$$
  \theta_{n+1} - \hat{\theta} = \frac{2}{9}(\theta_n - \hat{\theta}).
$$
The factor $2/9$ is the fraction of missing observations in this example.
